articles.title: US halts visa appointments globally amid Donald Trump's immigration crackdown
articles.summary: US News: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular offi.
articles.body: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular officers amid its broader immigration crackdown.A US State Department spokesperson said on Tuesday that the department had begun a training initiative at all US embassies and consulates worldwide. Visa appointment schedules will be adjusted to accommodate the training, the spokesperson said, according to Reuters.The State Department did not provide details on the training or specify how long the adjustments would last.It said the programme was aimed at helping consular officers screen applicants who could potentially become dependent on US public benefits and ensure that visa applications are evaluated "comprehensively and consistently".According to a Financial Times report, immigrant visa applicants with scheduled interviews at US embassies and consulates had received emails informing them that their appointments were being rescheduled and that they would be notified of new dates.The development comes as President Donald Trump's administration continues a broad immigration crackdown that has included visa and green-card revocations and the rejection of applications on various grounds, including political opinions and participation in pro-Palestinian protests.Trump has said the crackdown is intended to improve domestic security.Immigration crackdown faces legal challengesThe administration's immigration policies have also faced legal setbacks. A US judge on Friday struck down a policy that suspended the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, ruling that the measure exceeded secretary of state Marco Rubio's statutory authority.The administration has also moved to tighten restrictions on legal immigration.The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed making permanent a $103,265 fee for new cap-subject H-1B visa petitions, after a previous $100,000 fee imposed by Trump was blocked by a court.The proposed fee would significantly increase the cost for employers hiring foreign workers in specialised fields.The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers with specialised training. The programme provides 65,000 visas annually, along with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees.Trump's administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed changes to the visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers.Visa revocations add to pressure on applicantsThe administration is separately preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of potentially up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the US.The proposed action would cover B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought or are seeking asylum. The State Department is expected to announce the move in the coming weeks, according to news agency AP.B1 visas are generally issued for business travel, while B2 visas are generally used for tourism, family visits or medical treatment.The administration has also tightened screening requirements for visa applicants, including demands for additional information about their social media histories and, in some cases, expensive visa bonds.The latest pause in appointments therefore comes as the Trump administration continues to review and tighten several aspects of the US immigration and visa system.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Matthew Liberatore Hit Hard as Orioles Humiliate Cardinals Tuesday Night
articles.summary: Tuesday night was an opportunity for the St. Louis Cardinals to rebound from a profoundly disappointing end to the road trip returning home from Philadelphia...
articles.body:
Tuesday night was an opportunity for the St. Louis Cardinals to rebound from a profoundly disappointing end to the road trip returning home from Philadelphia , but would they? Much of that would depend on which version of Matthew Liberatore took the mound for the Cardinals. The answer is not the one most Cardinals fans were hoping for and the end result was appalling. Not to spoil this for you if you didn't see the game, but everyone in Busch Stadium that was not an Oriole's fan should demand their money back.

The game would get off to an auspicious start in the top of the 1st inning when Matthew Liberatore fielded Jackson Holliday 's dribbler on the 1st base side of the mound and fired the ball over Alec Burleson 's head into right field. Pete Alonso followed that with a solid single into left field with Holliday running on the play which gave the Orioles runners at first and third with no outs. Matthew would find a way out of the jam as he got Gunnar Henderson to pop out and then struck out Mayo and Encarnacion-Strand.

The top of the 3rd inning would be similar to the top of the 1st, but the result would be much different. Taveras reached as he beat out an infield hit. Jackson Holliday whistled a single into center which brought up Pete Alonzo who was not fooled by an 88 mph changeup which he sent soaring 435 feet deep into the left field stands for a 3-0 Baltimore lead. Two outs later, Encarnacion-Strand absolutely annihilated a 94 mph four-seam Liberatore fastball 450 feet even deeper into the left field stands for a 4-0 Orioles lead. That's the longest home run in Busch Stadium this season.

The Cardinals would not go away completely silently. Nathan Church waited on a 72 mph curveball from Orioles pitcher Chris Bassett and ripped it 405 feet into the Cardinals bullpen giving St. Louis a run making the score 4-1. That's the lone St. Louis Cardinals highlight, by the way.

That brief moment of St. Louis Cardinals optimism was short-lived. Matthew Liberatore would not survive the 5th inning. Jackson Holliday led off with his third hit of the night followed by another single from Cardinals nemesis Pete Alonzo. Matthew Liberatore then walked Gunnar Henderson to load the bases with no one out. Liberatore's last batter was Mayo who he surrendered a single to making it 5-1 Orioles and even though Matthew was done, Baltimore wasn't done scoring. Liberatore's replacement was Peter Strzelecki who didn't fare much better than his predecessor. He immediately gave up a single to Encarnacion-Strand which plated two more Orioles upping the Baltimore lead to 7-1. Stzelecki did accomplish one good thing during his relief outing. He struck out Basallo and…yeah, that's it. Next he hit Franklin with a pitch, gave up a single to Taveras, a single to Holliday and a double to Alonzo. When the dust settled, it was 12-1 Orioles and by the time the horrific 5th inning was done, Caleb Ferguson was in the game as the designated "you're pitching until you're too tired to pitch for the rest of the game" guy.

As many of the regulars for both teams sat going into the top of the 6th inning, the Orioles decided to score again just for fun when Ferguson gave up back-to-back doubles to Franklin and Beavers. 13-1 Baltimore. Someone please make it stop. Oh, did I say that out loud?

The Cardinals brought in Ryan Fernandez to take care of the Oriole's 7th inning. After Carlos Narvaez hit a double, it's almost like the Orioles had to try hard NOT to score. When Henderson grounded out, he seemed to just stroll to third as if he felt guilty about possibly scoring another run. Fortunately, Fernandez was able to get out of the inning without further humiliation. By contrast, the Orioles starter Chris Bassitt pitched deep into the bottom of the 7th inning when he was finally lifted for Baltimore reliever Cano.

Instead of going into any more details about the nuts and bolts of what happened for the start of the St. Louis Cardinals homestand, I can sum it up in 3 words: THAT. WAS. UGLY.

I'll add just one more thought before calling it a night. Was Matthew Liberatore's performance sub-par? Sure it was, but that's no excuse for what I perceived as an overall lack of energy from the St. Louis Cardinals Tuesday night. The fact that the game completely got out of hand in the 5th inning didn't help, but if they expect fans to fill the stands anytime soon, a better effort isn't just expected. It is demanded. I know it's a long season and we're nearing the end of it, but I'd like to see some resemblance of the young, hungry team we saw during the first couple of months. I started watching Tuesday night's game believing the Cardinals could muster a run to grab the third Wild Card slot. Now? Give me a break. Put a fork into this season. This team is done. I'd love to be proven wrong.

The St. Louis Cardinals will try again against the Baltimore Orioles Wednesday night. Michael McGreevy gets the start for the Cardinals while the Orioles will send Kyle Bradish to the mound. First pitch is scheduled for 6:45pm central time at Busch Stadium while the game broadcast is available via Cardinals.tv.

articles.title: Astros Outslug Yankees in 9-7 Victory
articles.summary: The Astros took their first bite out the big apple on Tuesday Night, and it was a big one. Astros 9 Yankees 7. Game one of the post-Dana Brown era had a diff...
articles.body:
The Astros took their first bite out the big apple on Tuesday Night, and it was a big one. Astros 9 Yankees 7.

Game one of the post-Dana Brown era had a different feel with a much-needed result. Call it desperation, call it sharper focus, patience at the plate, or just unwavering effort in erasing deficits. On this night, the Astros fought, and fought again, often manufacturing runs with two outs.

The scoring began in the Top of the 2nd. Yanier Diaz would take an inside first pitch fastball deep. That would be his 9th home run of the season, and the first of two Diaz would hit on the night.

The following frame, the Astros would increase their lead. Jose Altuve worked some two-out magic with a single, advancing on a passed ball and then came around to score on Dalton Varsho's single to left. That made things 2-0.

However, in the bottom of the third the Yankees would immediately place runners on the corners for Cody Bellinger , and with one swing he'd launch a 3-run blast to right field. For Ethan Pecko , it was his first allowed career HR in the majors.

The Astros would tie things up at 3-3 in the 5th. Yordan Alvarez would single to center, Paredes would walk and then once again with two outs Daulton Varsho would come through in the clutch with a single to right, scoring Alvarez.

Unfortunately, the tie would be broken in the bottom of the 5th with a Luis Garcia two-run shot that brought home Ben Rice who had reached with a walk. The Garcia homer would chase Pecko from the game. Pecko's final stat line on his 24th birthday read: IP 4.1 with 5 earned on 5 hits. He'd allow 4 walks, while registering a lone strike out against Austin Wells . Bennett Sousa would come on in relief authoring a bounce back effort, going 1.2 innings, setting down each batter in order.

In the 6th inning, Jeremy Pena would answer and tie things up yet again. Yanier Diaz drew a walk and then Pena would launch his 15th HR of the year to center field. Suddenly, the Astros had new life, an energy surge racing through the dugout.

Steven Okert would come in the 7th, making his 65th appearance on the year. Unfortunately, he'd leave a series of breaking balls high in the zone and the Yankees would seize the lead. Trent Grisham would walk, Ben Rice singled and then a double by Luis Garcia would make it 6-5. Okert's night was done. Bryan Abreu would close out the 7th.

In the 8th, Yanier Diaz would take advantage of the short porch in left, hitting his second solo shot of the night. That would tie things up 6-6. Pena would then reach on a single and he'd score when Yordan Alvarez dropped a triple into the gap. It would be his first triple of the season and his 91st RBI. Isaac Paredes would single home Yordan, and it was 8-6 heading into the bottom of the 8th.

In the bottom of the 8th, Manager Joe Espada elected to stick with Abreu. He'd promptly give up a double to Spencer Jones, who would come around and score on a single by Jazz Chisholm . Jose Caballero would reach on a single, and then Josh Hader for just the second time this season would be asked to pitch more than one inning.

He was up to the challenge. Hader would record the next four outs and has not allowed a run in his last 15 appearances. Exhale! Astros win. There are now exactly 30 games left in the season. The Astros added an insurance run in the 9th. They'd finish the night with 14 hits and would score in six different innings.

Mike Burrows , who last pitched on July 6th (bounced early by the Nationals), will finally return to the mound Wednesday Night in the Bronx. First pitch set for 6:05pm CDT.

Yankees SS George Lombard Jr. has now committed a throwing error in four straight games.

(Photo by Michael Urakami/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images

articles.title: Yordan Alvarez hits go-ahead triple in 8th inning as Astros outlast Yankees 9-7
articles.summary: Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesda...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesday night.

Yainer Diaz hit a pair of solo homers, including a tying shot to the short porch in right field off Headrick's fastball to start the eighth. After Jeremy Pena singled, Alvarez ripped a low-inside sinker to the warning track in right-center for a 7-6 lead.

Alvarez increased his major league-leading batting average to .323. The slugger had his seventh career triple and first since July 21, 2024.

Pena homered off Fernando Cruz in the sixth for a 5-all tie. Daulton Varsho had two RBI singles for the Astros, who won for the sixth time in 15 games after owner Jim Crane said manager Joe Espada will finish the season.

Isaac Paredes added an RBI single off Headrick (7-3), who has allowed five homers in 68 appearances. Headrick is second in the big leagues in appearances to Toronto lefty Mason Fluharty and permitted a run for only the 12th time.

Diaz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth off rookie Bradley Hanner as the Astros scored six runs against New York's bullpen.

Houston overcame a four-hit night by New York first baseman Luis García Jr. García hit an RBI double off Steven Okert that gave the Yankees a 6-5 lead and also launched a two-run homer in the fifth off rookie starter Ethan Packo.

It was García's third four-hit game this season and the eighth of his career.

Bryan Abreu (5-3) allowed an RBI single to Jazz Chisholm Jr. before finishing a double play against Austin Wells with a nice grab at first base. Josh Hader got four outs for his 19th save in 19 chances.

Cody Bellinger hit a three-run homer in the third that broke a 32-game homerless drought and gave the Yankees a 3-2 lead.

Packo allowed five runs and five hits in 4 1/3 innings on his 24th birthday.

New York starter Will Warren permitted three runs — two earned — and seven hits in five innings.

Astros RHP Peter Lambert (8-7, 3.68 ERA) pitches Wednesday night. The Yankees had not announced a scheduled starter.

articles.title: Jalen Duren’s $160M Pistons Deal Could Finally End Lengthy Contract Standstill
articles.summary: Jalen Duren has been a restricted free agent for quite some time. The Detroit Pistons have tried to negotiate a contract with the one-time All-Star since fre...
articles.body:
Jalen Duren has been a restricted free agent for quite some time. The Detroit Pistons have tried to negotiate a contract with the one-time All-Star since free agency began. Initially, the starting center wanted to ink a five-year, $287.1 million deal with Detroit. However, the franchise has been hesitant to give Duren a massive payday.

Duren is coming off an outstanding season for the Pistons, where he appeared in 70 games , averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 assists. He was named an All-Star for the first time in his career and was named to the All-NBA Third Team. He feels he should be compensated fairly based on his improvement.

Unfortunately for Duren, the Pistons have been hesitant to give him a massive deal. Mostly because of how he underperformed in the postseason. He averaged 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds during the playoffs. The star big man was not a key factor in Detroit's short postseason run.

Despite the lengthy contract standstill , NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that Jalen Duren could still sign and stay in Detroit.

"We still have about a month left for restricted free agents to come to terms with their incumbent teams," Fischer said . "I talked with someone today who still believes he's on track for a four-year, $160 million deal. He's clearly gonna want something closer to what Walker Kessler got than what Mitchell Robinson got. But when all things are said and done, and he makes life-changing money, I do see an opportunity for this to get mended."

At the start of free agency, Jalen Duren was linked to the Sacramento Kings and Los Angeles Lakers .

Jalen Duren's Contract Talks With the Pistons Turned "Nasty"

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons want different things in their contract negotiation. According to ESPN's Tim MacMahon on "The Hoop Collective," things have turned sour in their ongoing bargaining.

"What's going to be the lingering cloud when this whole Jalen Duren situation gets finalized, or at least temporarily settled? Is he going to sign an extension? I don't know. This has been an awfully nasty negotiation, and I have real concerns there," the insider said .

Duren's situation has become tricky since no team would want to sign him. Additionally, most teams have used their cap space, and the only way for the big man to be with a different team would be through a sign-and-trade agreement.

Fortunately for Duren, their recent contract talks have turned into something positive.

articles.title: ‘People can think what they want': Wyndham Clark responds to rules ‘scrutiny'
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark, at the Tour Championship, responds to rules "scrutiny" after a move at the BMW Championship.
articles.body:
Wyndham Clark says he didn't take "a bad lie and make it good."

And if you think that he did during Sunday's final round of the BMW Championship?

"People can think what they want," Clark said.

His comments came Tuesday ahead of this week's Tour Championship , where he was asked about a scene to the right of the 14th hole at Bellerive Country Club, host of the BMW. There, while Clark prepared to hit his second shot on the par-4, a CBS camera positioned to his right caught the following:

– Clark grabbed an iron from his bag, placed it behind his ball, then took a practice swing just to the left of the ball. Twice more, he placed his iron behind the ball and took practice swings, before going back to his bag for a different iron. At the time, Clark was tied for the lead with Rory McIlroy.

– CBS cut away to Gary Woodland on the 15th hole.

– When it returned, Clark was placing an iron behind his ball. He then took another practice swing to the left of it before his caddie, David Pelekoudas, moved between Clark and the camera, though another practice swing could be seen. Clark then went back to his bag for a different iron. Three times, he placed that iron behind his ball and took practice swings. At about this point, CBS analysts said the following:

Trevor Immelman: "He's taking a long look at this. This is like the third club that he's placed down behind the ball there."

Frank Nobilo: "So the lie might be better."

From there, Clark placed his 9-iron behind the ball and hit, finished the hole with a par and went on to win by three . But Nobilo's comment, along with several similar remarks on social media, is interesting. Did Clark improve his lie? On Tuesday, Clark was asked the following question:

Wyndham, your drive on 14 Sunday went into the right rough, and there was a lot of scrutiny on social media but also even the TV announcers. Curious about you changing clubs and tapping down the rough multiple times. Just curious what you were thinking there, and there was a similar situation possibly at the U.S. Open, and if you've been hearing about this at all.

"I didn't really hear much about it," Clark said. "I know the shot that you're talking about. I think any player, when they're trying to judge a lie, takes out different clubs to see what it feels like.

"I never fully put the club down behind it. I don't think anything of it."

Match play included in PGA Tour's radically new postseason structure

As part of his answer, he also noted a pair of previous incidents in which his actions around the ball have been questioned — during the third round of the 2024 Arnold Palmer Invitational , Clark placed his iron behind his ball, causing the grass and ball to move, though no rules penalty was assessed; then, at this year's U.S. Open , a video of Clark stepping on the grass around his ball circulated online. On Tuesday, Clark also brought up the actions of Bryson DeChambeau at this year's Open Championship, where DeChambeau was penalized for improving the area around his intended swing.

"When the cameras are on you, they're going to find anything," Clark said. "And I think you saw that in Bryson's case. It happened to me at the U.S. Open, it happened to me at Bay Hill. It's happened to a lot of guys where they can see stuff that maybe looks like something that maybe it's not."

Rule 8.1b (4) states that players are allowed to, "ground the club lightly right in front of or right behind the ball," with "ground the club lightly" meaning, "allowing the weight of the club to be supported by the grass, soil, sand or other material on or above the ground surface."

"That lie was never bad," Clark said Tuesday. "It was more just judging what it was. By no means did I take a bad lie and make it really good.

"People can think what they want. I know I didn't do anything that was costing the integrity of the field. That's all I've got to say about that."

articles.title: Mets, behind Thornton and Lindor, beat Brewers in extras
articles.summary: The Mets walk it off in ten.
articles.body:
It was a back and forth night in Queens, but the Mets emerged on top, taking game one of this series with the Milwaukee Brewers , winning 3-2 in extras. After losing two of three in walkoff fashion to the White Sox , the Mets held on to win a game late and continued their post-deadline hot streak.

The Mets got yet another quality start of our their young pitching tonight, with Zac Thornton continuing his improbable run of success. Over six runs, Thornton didn't walk a batter, allowed seven hits, induced two ground ball double plays, and struck out four. He worked himself out of trouble, he limited damage, and he continues to look like he absolutely belongs in the big leagues after being nowhere near anyone's radar at season's start.

His most impressive inning might've been the third, which started out with two straight base hits to the left side of the infield. A comebacker to the mound resulted in the first out coming at third base. A fly ball and a groundout got Thornton out of the inning and was another's illustration of how he's able to buckle down and not let game circumstances get the best of him.

The only blemish against him came in the fourth inning, when William Contreras led off the inning with a double and was driven in by a two-out single by Luis Lara.

The Mets got their offense off the long ball, with both Francisco Lindor and Luis Robert Jr. depositing balls over the left-field wall. Lindor's dinger was the only run scored against starter Kyle Harrison , who is having a spectacular year, and looked quite good in his five innings of work as well. He struck out five, walked one, and gave up six hits. His slurve was especially effective early on and he, like Thornton, looked in control with just about every pitch he threw.

Robert's home run came off of Chad Patrick , who was the first out of the bullpen for the Brewers. Robert let go of the bat with one hand and looked like he was swinging at maybe 50% intensity, and the ball still traveled over the Great Wall of Flushing. Antonio Senzatela was up next, and was good in his inning and a third of work. Aaron Ashby didn't allow a baserunner in his one-inning of work.

On the Mets' side, Nate Lavender relieved Thornton, and he was great in his two innings of work, not allowing a baserunner and keeping batters off-balance. Tonight's six batters faced was officially the longest outing of Lavender's career thus far.

Austin Warren got the save opportunity tonight for the Mets, and William Contreras greeted him rudely by doubling on the third pitch of the at-bat. Pinch hitter Jake Bauers was up next, and he drew a four-pitch walk. Christian Yelich pinch hit next, and lined a ball the other way to drive in Contreras with the tying run. After getting Lara to strike out for the first out, that was it for Warren.

Friday night's goat Jefry Yan was brought in to try to close out the inning with the game tied to face lefty Garrett Mitchell , and he got the strikeout on a challenged call. Joey Ortiz then walked to load the bases, bringing up David Hamilton as the batter to either end the half-frame or drive in the winning run. Hamilton laced a ball to the left side, but a stretched-out Lindor snagged the ball out of the air to keep the game tied.

[Side note: it appears that the MLB.tv feed went out as the ball was in the air, sending a gasp across the tri-state area]

Trevor Megill , brother of the felled Tylor, pitched the ninth for the Milwaukee. After quickly dispatching Luis Torrens and A.J. Ewing, the hero of the last half inning—Lindor—came up, and hit a perfectly placed single down the third base line for an infield single. However, he was caught leaning off of first base, and was picked off to end the inning.

Jonathan Pintaro started the tenth, and struck out Jackson Chourio to start things off. Bruce Turang was next, same result, a swinging strikeout. Contreras was up next, and he worked the count full before taking his base. However, Pintaro got Bauers to fly out to end the frame without a run scoring.

Bo Bichette led off the bottom of the tenth against Megill with a fly ball to center. That would bring up Carson Benge, who already had three hits, and was intentionally walked to put two on for Robert. Robert showcased an eye at the plate that isn't always there and drew a walk to load the bases.

Christopher Morel strode to the plate, just a few innings after Gary Cohen mentioned how positive of a clubhouse presence he is, and grounded into what looked to be a sure out to third base, However, David Hamilton made an errant to throw to home, allowing Lindor to score and the Mets to take game one of the series.

Robert Stock takes the ball tomorrow for the Mets, and will face Dustin May for the middle game of this series.

According to offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb, the offensive line's five starters are almost set.

"I think we're close," Grubb said. "We're right to game week, and it's been pretty consistently the same five."

He singled out the left guard battle as one that will come down to sophomore Mal Waldrep and junior Will Sanders.

articles.title: Francisco Lindor keys Mets' walk-off win over Brewers
articles.summary: NEW YORK — The Mets had a one-run lead coming into the top of the ninth, but right-hander Austin Warren put the first two hitters on base before giving up a...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The Mets had a one-run lead coming into the top of the ninth, but right-hander Austin Warren put the first two hitters on base before giving up a game-tying RBI double to pinch-hitter Christian Yelich .

Warren, who recently came off the injured list after dealing with forearm tightness, blew what would have been his first save of the season, and was pulled with just one out.

With two outs and the bases loaded, Francisco Lindor snared a line drive by David Hamilton to keep the game tied.

In the bottom of the 10th, Trevor Megill , the brother of injured Mets starter Tylor Megill , got the first out, then intentionally walked Carson Benge, and walked Luis Robert Jr. to load the bases. Christopher Morel hit a chopper to third base, but Hamilton's throw was off target. Lindor came home safe, and the Mets walked off in the 3-2 series opening win.

This came after Left-hander Nate Lavender tossed two scoreless innings in relief, continuing his impressive rookie streak. He hasn't allowed a run in nine innings and has given up only one hit, walked two hitters and struck out 11.

Left-hander Zac Thornton pitched well enough to give the Mets a chance to win, and after giving up a run with two outs in the top of the fourth, Lindor helped him out in the bottom of the fifth with a game-tying home run off left-hander Kyle Harrison (one earned run on six hits, five strikeouts over five innings).

Robert put the Mets ahead 2-1 with a shot off right-hander Chad Patrick in the bottom of the sixth, leading off with his 10th of the season.

Thornton went six innings, holding the NL Central's first-place to team to one run on seven hits, and struck out four.

articles.title: Gao Zhen: China jails artist over satirical Mao Zedong sculptures, say rights groups
articles.summary: The case against Gao Zhen, who was prosecuted under a law banning "slander of heroes", has been seen as an assault on artistic freedom.
articles.body:
A Chinese artist known for his satirical sculptures of Mao Zedong has been handed a maximum three-year jail term for "slandering China's heroes", according to rights groups.

A court in Hebei province had ruled on Tuesday that Gao Zhen's work "infringes upon the hero's reputation and harms public interest".

Among the 70-year-old's most famous pieces, produced with his brother Gao Qiang, is a sculpture comprising a squad of Mao-like figures holding Jesus Christ at gunpoint.

Gao has been in detention for the past two years, and the UN and many rights groups have called for him to be released. Amnesty International has called his sentencing an "assault" on artistic freedom.

Gao had moved to the US in 2022 but was arrested at his studio on the outskirts of Beijing during a visit in August 2024.

Authorities seized his artworks and barred his wife and seven-year-old son from leaving China.

China watchers have said that Gao Zhen's arrest shows how the Chinese Communist Party is becoming increasingly extreme in both grasp and reach – including by policing its citizens transnationally and retroactively.

He was charged under a law that came into force in March 2018, which bans the defamation of historical figures associated with the party.

The Gao brothers' Execution of Christ sculpture was exhibited in 2009, as were two other sculptures cited in the case.

They are Mao's Guilt, a life-sized replica of the leader kneeling in a pose of solemn contrition; and Miss Mao which depicts him with large breasts and a long, Pinocchio-style nose.

Gao's case was heard in a one-day, closed-door trial earlier this year, which received limited coverage in China.

He plans to appeal the conviction, Amnesty International said on Tuesday.

If the verdict is upheld, Gao would be due to complete his sentence in August 2027 as it would take into account the two years that he has already spent in detention.

"No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history," Amnesty International's China Director Sarah Brooks said on Tuesday.

"This trial demonstrates how broadly worded and politically motivated laws are used – and worse, in this case, used retroactively – to silence artists, activists and other individuals who dare to express views that differ from those of the Chinese government," she said.

"The case against [Gao Zhen] raises particular concerns with regard to the retroactive application of criminal law, the use of criminal sanctions to punish artistic expression, and the impact on his family," the UN's Human Rights Office told AFP news agency.

Earlier this year, his brother Gao Qiang told the BBC that the trial's "message is clear".

"Even if a work was made 15 years ago, it can still be turned into a crime if today's political climate changes," he said.

articles.title: From ‘ridiculous’ to a viral success: Akron’s offensive coordinator contest has been a big hit
articles.summary: Some people thought Andrew Goodrich was bonkers when he suggested that the University of Akron hold a contest to name an “Offensive Coordinator of the Game”...
articles.body:
AKRON, Ohio (AP) — Some people thought Andrew Goodrich was bonkers when he suggested that the University of Akron hold a contest to name an "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" for its home opener against Robert Morris on Sept. 12.

But after the Zips' athletic director explained and refined the idea, the promotion has turned out to be a public relations success and a revenue driver.

Akron garnered 23 million social media views and an influx of new season ticket-holders since the contest was announced Aug. 4.

"I just wanted to do something that no one had ever done before. And maybe more importantly than that, I wanted to do something that would make fans read that and look at their friend and go, 'Are you serious? Would I really have a chance to do this?' And that's what we were looking for," Goodrich said. "We thought it would be popular in our backyard of maybe the MAC, northeast Ohio and western Pennsylvania. We didn't realize that the whole world was going to go, 'Hey, you know what? We love this.'"

Marty Whims II, a longtime season ticket-holder, was announced as the winner Tuesday. Whims graduated from Akron and is the chief financial officer for Stark Enterprises.

Akron's College of Business and the George W. Daverio School of Accountancy conducted the random drawing.

"It's a unique opportunity. The football program benefits from season tickets and then shines us in a positive light. I never had on my bingo card that I'd be on TMZ Sports," coach Joe Moorhead said. "Like I told our players when they heard about it, I said, 'I'm not going to let the circus roll into town. It ain't happening under my watch.' It's going to give somebody a unique opportunity, but I'm never going to make a mockery of the game or disrespect our opponent."

Whims will get to call one series. Moorhead's sheet for the opening series includes 12 to 24 plays.

The idea was formed during a plane trip back from March Madness

Goodrich first had the idea on a flight from Tampa, Florida, after the Zips were eliminated by Texas Tech in the first round of the NCAA men's basketball tournament on March 20.

Senior deputy AD and chief operating officer Matt Pottorff told Goodrich it was a terrible idea when he first heard it, until they discussed it more.

Letting a fan be an OC for an entire game was a nonstarter and calling one play wasn't enough of a selling point. Calling one series, though, was a happy medium.

Pottorff said the two biggest issues that remained were getting buy-in from Coach Moorhead and announcing it when it would get more attention.

"We wanted to be just basically at the right time with ticket sales and ticket staff," Pottorff said. "We had kind of all hands on deck at this point to make sure everybody's ready. But we didn't think that this was going to be anywhere near as huge as it ended up being."

Moorhead, who is his own offensive coordinator, was initially skeptical.

"At first I thought it was absolutely ridiculous. I don't even let my assistant coaches call plays. I call the plays," he said. "As we talked through it a little bit more and discussed some of the guardrails and parameters where, 'Hey, this guy's not bringing in a single-wing playbook and putting it in Friday before the game.' He's going to come in, you'll walk them through what's in the game plan. You'll talk about, 'Hey, this is what Robert Morris plays in all these different situations. Here's my opening script for the game. What are your ideas? And then, hey, what do you think about this play in this position?' And make it more of a collaboration, for lack of a better term."

Only those with season tickets or suites were eligible for the contest. Besides new season-ticket sales, suites sold out for the first time since InfoCision Stadium opened in 2009. Jon Gruden, Pat McAfee and Dan "Big Cat" Katz ended up ponying up for season tickets, as well as fans from 38 states and as far away as Germany.

Every season and suite ticket counted as an entry (four tickets, four entries). Season ticket-holders also received additional entries for each new season ticket buyer they referred.

The nine finalists were announced Aug. 19, including Katz of Barstool Sports, longtime season ticket-holders, and people from Nebraska and Texas.

The promotion even got a last-minute corporate sponsor with fast-food chain Arby's coming aboard.

articles.title: Pete Alonso homers and drives in 4 before leaving game as Orioles rout Cardinals 13-1
articles.summary: Pete Alonso had four hits, including a three-run homer, and drove in four runs before leaving the game in the fifth inning, and the Baltimore Orioles routed...
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS (AP) — Pete Alonso had four hits, including a three-run homer, and drove in four runs before leaving the game in the fifth inning, and the Baltimore Orioles routed the swooning St. Louis Cardinals 13-1 on Tuesday night.

Chris Bassitt (5-4) allowed one run on six hits in 6 2/3 innings, matching his longest start of the season. He struck out five and walked none as the Orioles, who are chasing an AL wild-card spot, won for the third time in four games.

The Cardinals lost their fourth straight.

Alonso, who has been dealing with a nagging calf injury, left shortly after he contributed his fourth hit, an RBI double during Baltimore's eight-run fifth that made it 12-1. He put the Orioles ahead 3-0 with his 435-foot shot in the third off Matthew Liberatore (5-12), his 31st of the season.

Jackson Holliday had three hits, scored twice and drove in a run for the Orioles in his first big league appearance in St. Louis, where his father, Matt, starred for the Cardinals. Christian Encarnacion-Strand had a pair of hits, including a 450-foot homer in the third, and drove in three. Leody Taveras had two hits, scored twice and drove in two runs.

Liberatore allowed a season-high eight runs on eight hits in four-plus innings. He struck out seven and walked one.

Nathan Church homered for the Cardinals. Alec Burleson extended his hitting streak to 11 games, the longest active streak in the National League, with a sixth-inning single.

Pedro Pagés pitched a scoreless ninth. It was the second time in the last three games that the Cardinals catcher closed out a game on the mound.

Orioles RHP Kyle Bradish (7-12, 3.70 ERA) will face Cardinals RHP Michael McGreevy (5-9, 3.54) on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Jets Receive Alarming Concerns After Practice
articles.summary: The New York Jets received some alarming concerns about the offensive line after the final training camp practice. The post Jets Receive Alarming Concerns Af...
articles.body:
The New York Jets received some alarming concerns from the final training camp practice.

Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic said on Tuesday, August 25, "By my count, the Jets backup O-Line has allowed five sacks today with Cade Klubnik at QB."

Rosenblatt wasn't the only one who noticed the shoddy play from the backups in the trenches.

"Jets backup O-line: Pass protection is leaky (understatement). Klubnik has held the ball at times but too many free rushers," ESPN's Rich Cimini posted on X.

Analyst Is Concerned With This Potential Foreshadowing

In the Week 2, 17-0 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers , the Jets allowed four sacks.

ESPN New York's Jake Asman didn't like what he saw from the backup linemen that suited up in that contest.

"Some negatives I have in my notes, and we kind of alluded to it when I talked about [Cade] Klubnik. He was under way too much pressure. The second team and third team offensive line, not very good. Now I get it, most teams probably have bad offensive lines besides their starters. The Jets last year were remarkably healthy on the offensive line. They were, we can call it for what it is. Last year, the New York Jets started the same five guys for all 17 games. Now, yes, Alijah Vera-Tucker got hurt on the Tuesday before Week 1, I get it, but they didn't have another injury to their offensive line. The odds of that happening again two years in a row feel unlikely, right?" Asman openly asked.

"I don't think they have great offensive line depth, especially in the interior … I think the backup offensive line, eh, I don't know if you can feel great about it … The Jets better hope the starting offensive line stays healthy because the depth behind it is not going to inspire a whole lot of confidence," Asman bluntly stated.

The Jets had a defensive tackle issue last season. It was abundantly clear throughout the entire offseason. Right before the start of the 2025 campaign, general manager Darren Mougey solved the problem.

He pulled off a pair of savvy trades to acquire Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs to fortify the position. Could Mougey make lightning strike in the same place twice?

The defensive tackle position is one of the deepest on the Jets' roster ahead of 2026, but the same can't be said for the other side of the trenches. However, the problem is that every team in the NFL doesn't have enough offensive line depth.

The supply of good linemen is always low, and the demand is always sky-high.

So if Mougey is going to pull a rabbit out of the hat, it'll be more difficult than last year. The brutally honest conversation is the Jets' depth in the trenches is going to get tested this year; it's a near guarantee.

The Jets were the only team in the NFL last year that started the same five guys on the offensive line. Gang Green hadn't accomplished that feat as an organization since 2012.

They're unlikely to pull that off in back-to-back years. That means the Jets' depth on the O-Line better be on point, or else the issues in training camp could be some serious foreshadowing for the season to come.

articles.title: Morgan Scalley just wrapped up his first fall camp as the Utes’ head coach. Here are the takeaways
articles.summary: Here's what stood out as the Utah Utes wrapped up fall camp.
articles.body:
Utah concluded fall camp on Saturday and has shifted into preparation for the season opener against Idaho on Sept. 3.

Football season is close, and Utah's players are fired up to play against someone other than their own teammates.

"I'm just excited to hit someone else other than my teammates and the people that I love around me," said linebacker Trey Reynolds. "Excited to take it out on some other people."

One of the biggest takeaways for coach Morgan Scalley is that his team got through fall camp "injury free for the most part." That hasn't always been the case at Utah, so Scalley is pleased with where the team is at as August draws to a close

"We got some bumps and bruises, guys that still need to get some rehab in, but we'll be ready to go for Game 1 and feel very good about where we're at in terms of depth chart and stuff like that — stuff I won't talk to you guys about," Scalley said.

With fall camp finished, the Utes now turn their attention to Idaho. That includes watching offensive film of Grand Valley State , where Vandals offensive coordinator Ian Shoemaker is coming from, and defensive film of Iowa State, where Idaho defensive coordinator Lee Stalker was a defensive assistant.

Idaho opens the season this Friday against Cal Poly.

"You're trying to get any sort of information you can get from where these coaches are coming from. The good news is they'll be playing on Friday, so we'll get a really good peek at that. But just making sure your guys understand how to study film the right way," Scalley said.

Utah accomplished what it needed to this fall camp, establishing the depth chart and improving tackling while staying injury-free for the most part.

One area of improvement from Utah's first scrimmage of fall camp was red zone efficiency. After the closed-to-the-media scrimmage, Scalley had this to say:

"I'd say red-zone work, kind of a mixed bag. We need to be more efficient, not enough touchdowns in the red zone, too many field goals," Scalley said.

It's safe to say that OC Kevin McGiven and the rest of the offense heard that message, as the red zone success rate was up to close camp.

"I'm glad I said that because maybe they got butthurt or something because it's been fantastic since then. So maybe they thought I was calling them out. Man, really good the next couple days. That was fantastic," Scalley said. "McGiven is a competitor, man. Maybe he heard that and was like, 'OK'. No, that was good. Yeah, we've cleaned some stuff up for sure."

As part of the march toward the start of the season, Utah announced its captains and leadership committee for 2026.

Quarterback Devon Dampier , running back Wayshawn Parker , offensive lineman Alex Harrison, linebackers Jonathan Hall and Trey Reynolds and safety Nate Ritchie were named captains.

Along with the captains, defensive ends Lance Holtzclaw and Ethan Day, safety Jackson Bennee , offensive lineman Zereoue Williams, defensive tackle Karson Kaufusi, safety Rabbit Evans, long snapper Logan Castor, tight end Noah Bennee, quarterback Byrd Ficklin , wide receivers Tobias Merriweather and Braden Pegan and linebacker Cyrus Polu were named to the team's leadership council.

"You can see it's a big one, right? You've got a big leadership council. You got a lot of guys getting a lot of votes. That's a good thing. There's not one guy in that group, whether it be from the captain group or the leadership council groups that you're going, 'Oh no.' Those guys are compelling. They're bringing others with them. It's a really solid group," Scalley said.

Here are three other takeaways as the Utes wrapped up fall camp

Utah feels like it has a very deep wide receiver room this year, with Kyri Shoels, Larry Simmons, Creed Whittemore, Ricky Johnson , Tobias Merriweather and Mana Carvalho all potentially having roles depending on the opponent and defensive matchup.

"For the first time in a long time, we've had so many good receivers to help our corners at all positions," said cornerbacks coach Sharrieff Shah.

Utah State transfer Braden Pegan, who transferred from Utah State, should be the group's WR1.

After catching 60 balls from Bryson Barnes for 926 yards and five touchdowns last season in Kevin McGiven's offense, Pegan could be a favorite target of quarterback Devon Dampier.

The 6-foot-3, 210-pound junior is one of the tallest players in the receiver room and has put that height to good use in his ability to snag 50-50 balls. While he's a big target for Dampier, he also has plenty of speed and was a threat from all over the field. He has sure hands, too, dropping just two balls on 94 targets.

If Pegan's fall camp performance is any indication, he could have a big season for the Utes.

"If Braden Pegan does what he's been doing to us, which I believe he will … It not only frustrates you, but you recognize that, all right, if we get a fifty fifty ball from him, we've done good. We've done good," said cornerbacks coach Sharieff Shah.

Utah feels confident in offensive line travel group, but still needs to decide on starting five

The good news for offensive line coach Jordan Gross is that he feels that he has 10 players that he's confident in playing in a Big 12 game.

"It's been an outstanding fall camp. All the credit goes to our players on that offensive line. Everything from no returning starters to a new offense to a new O-line coach, there's just so much that they've had to take on and every day has been just even more encouragement to me that they are all in on being a really great unit this year," Gross said.

The Utes, of course, replace all five starters from last season's fantastic offensive line, and finding the right combination of players for Utah's first game has been one of the key storylines in fall camp.

While the Utes have a great idea of who those five will be, Gross is still finalizing that starting unit.

"Honestly, still working to identify who that first five will be when we take the field. And that's a very good thing. Not, 'Oh crap, who is it going to be? Dang it, who do I need to pick out of this unit?' So been a lot of fun. I'm very lucky. It's a great group," Gross said.

Alex Harrison, Zereoue Williams, Keith Olson, Solatoa Moea'i, Kelvin Obot, Isaiah Garcia and Cedric Jefferson are expected to at least be in the rotation. Which combination of those players will start is still to be determined, and could even change after the first game if the starting group isn't playing the way they need to.

Byrd Ficklin's role will be fascinating to watch

After last season, Utah coaches are not going to let Byrd Ficklin sit idly on the sidelines. Not after directly contributing to three Ute wins and rushing for 513 yards and three touchdowns last year.

"A lot of explosiveness. A lot of explosive plays. Even when I'm on or off the field, no matter what's going to happen, something exciting is going to be on the field," Ficklin said. "Every player is going to be exciting, a lot of speed, a lot of gos, everything."

Utah has largely kept the specifics of Ficklin's offensive involvement under wraps, but he will see the field plenty this year in a variety of different positions, including some packages with Dampier at quarterback.

"I think with Byrd, it's utilization. How can you contribute and what does that look like?" McGiven said this spring. "He's like a Swiss army knife and without giving up the ship, there's a lot of different things that he can do on a play-to-play basis and different places that he can line up. And we need to be able to utilize those and get creative with those packages."

articles.title: Orioles clobber Cardinals, 13-1, behind Holliday’s table-setting, Alonso’s power
articles.summary: ST. LOUIS — A few hours before the Orioles’ series opener against the Cardinals, Jackson Holliday spoke about what he expected it to feel like to play in the...
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS — A few hours before the Orioles' series opener against the Cardinals , Jackson Holliday spoke about what he expected it to feel like to play in the ballpark where he grew up watching his dad play.

The last time Holliday hit at Busch Stadium was when he was 12 years old. A decade later, Holliday said he was going to focus on putting one out during batting practice first.

"I'll try my best in BP, start there," the leadoff hitter said. "Hopefully, get a few knocks this week."

Holliday sparked the Orioles' offense to one of its most impressive outputs of the season — and the ballcub to one of its best victories of the year — by smacking three of the team's 16 hits en route to Baltimore 's 13-1 win. The offensive output is tied for the Orioles' highest this season, while their 12-run margin of victory is their best of the year.

But Holliday, whose parents and grandparents were in attendance, might not have been the happiest player on the Orioles to be in St. Louis this week. Pete Alonso , the Orioles' No. 2 hitter, entered with Ruthian numbers at Busch Stadium, and they became even more like The Great Bambino's after the Polar Bear's 4-for-4 performance.

Alonso blasted a three-run homer in the third inning and then smacked two more hits to follow Holliday in the fifth to keep the quarter in the merry-go-round of Baltimore's season-best eight-run frame. Alonso's 1.243 OPS at Busch Stadium is the best of any player with at least 75 plate appearances in the ballpark, and it's the slugger's best at any MLB stadium in which he has at least 50 plate appearances.

In total, Holliday and Alonso combined for seven hits, four runs, five RBIs and two extra-base hits.

The blowout win starts a pivotal nine-game road trip off on a much-needed high note. The Orioles (64-68) are temporarily two games back of the Cleveland Guardians for the third and final wild-card spot in the mediocre American League. Baltimore's next eight games come against a Cardinals team that's now below .500, the AL-worst Athletics and the NL-worst Rockies.

Long before the offensive outburst, the first inning had a feeling of deja vu for Baltimore's bats. Holliday reached base on an error and advanced to third on an Alonso single, but they were stranded after three straight Orioles failed to hit the ball out of the infield against Cardinals left-hander Matthew Liberatore .

Two innings later, the Orioles got runners on the corners again thanks to a Leody Taveras single and a perfectly executed hit-and-run between the outfielder and Holliday, and Alonso ensured it wouldn't go to waste by clobbering a 435-foot long ball — his 31st of the season — to left-center field. The big fly continued Alonso's scorching-hot stretch since the trade deadline, during which he's hit an eye-popping .416 with a 1.237 OPS. Christian Encarnacion-Strand , a lefty masher who's helped the Orioles improve against southpaws since he joined the team in mid-July, then put Baltimore up 4-0.

The explosion in the fifth began with the first five batters — and nine of the first 10 — reaching base. Coby Mayo hit a 107 mph line drive off shortstop JJ Wetherholt's glove for an RBI single to knock Liberatore out of the game. Encarnacion-Strand then hit a ground ball with eyes for a two-run single to put the Orioles up 7-1.

Taveras, one of the Orioles' best hitters with runners in scoring position this season, delivered with a two-run single with the bases loaded, followed by an RBI single from Holliday and an RBI double from Alonso to put the Orioles ahead 12-1. Baltimore tacked on another run in the sixth on back-to-back doubles from Christian Franklin and Dylan Beavers .

Manager Craig Albernaz then pulled Alonso, who has been managing a calf injury over the past 10 days, in the bottom of the fifth.

The victory wasn't just because of the offense, though. Chris Bassitt was steady throughout the evening to deliver 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball. The long run came on a Nathan Church solo homer in the third.

The start was perhaps Bassitt's best of the season — one that was marred by back pain and then surgery to fix it. But the 37-year-old right-hander, who was signed for $18.5 million to stabilize the rotation, has delivered three straight solid starts since returning from the injured list.

The Orioles will look to take the series Wednesday with ace Kyle Bradish on the mound opposite Cardinals right-hander Michael McGreevy .
authors: Jacob Calvin Meyer, The Baltimore Sun

articles.title: ‘They Don’t Deserve To Be Agitated’ — Stephen A. Smith Rips ‘Classless’ Enes Kanter for Dragging WNBA Players Into Trans Stunt
articles.summary: The aftermath of Sunday’s viral confrontation between Enes Kanter and Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud is still unfolding. Kanter was sitting courtside at Chi...
articles.body:
The aftermath of Sunday's viral confrontation between Enes Kanter and Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud is still unfolding. Kanter was sitting courtside at Chicago's Wintrust Arena when he got into a verbal spat with the veteran guard, drawing strong reactions from around the WNBA.

On Tuesday, Stephen A. Smith weighed in on the incident and took issue with Kanter's decision to involve WNBA players in the broader transgender athlete debate.

Stephen A. Smith Slams Enes Kanter for Involving WNBA Players in Transgender Controversy

Kanter made headlines earlier this month when he announced his intention to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. After identifying himself as a "woman," he argued that the league's CBA does not clearly define the term and that he should therefore be eligible.

On Sunday, Kanter attended the Sky's game against the Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read: "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

But his appearance quickly became more than a statement.

According to Sky owner Michael Alter on Tuesday, Kanter provoked Cloud into a heated exchange that ultimately led arena security to escort him from the building.

Smith addressed the confrontation on his "Straight Shooter" podcast, saying Kanter crossed a line by directing the controversy toward players who were simply trying to play basketball.

"I think on one hand Enes Kanter was very wrong. It was a classless thing for him to do because the ladies that are playing don't have anything to do with this. They have nothing to do with this, and they don't deserve to be agitated," Smith said .

Kanter has become a prominent voice in the debate over whether transgender women should compete in women's sports. His position is similar to that of Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham , who has also faced significant criticism for her views.

Kanter has publicly supported Cunningham and reportedly directed some of that attention toward Cloud during Sunday's game.

Smith said he understands the broader point Kanter is trying to make. The ESPN personality also backed Cunningham's position earlier this summer. But he drew a line between expressing an opinion and bringing the players into the middle of the fight.

For Smith, the issue is not whether Kanter can voice his position. It is how he chose to do it. He argued that WNBA players should not have to deal with the fallout from a debate that the league should have definitively addressed.

SEE ALSO: 'He Made Himself Into a Threat' – Sky Owner Blasts Enes Kanter For Playing the Victim Card During Natasha Cloud Incident

The Sky has since taken its own position. Alter announced that Kanter has been banned from the team's home games, adding another layer to an already contentious situation.

Kanter, however, disputes the idea that he went to the arena looking for a confrontation. Appearing on Fox News on Monday, he said Cloud was the one who started screaming at him and maintained that he was there to support Cunningham and "protect women."

The disagreement now comes down to two very different accounts of the same incident. What is clear is that Kanter's WNBA campaign has moved well beyond a draft declaration, with the Cloud confrontation turning his message into a league-wide controversy.

articles.title: Astros beat Yankees 9-7 as Alvarez hits a go-ahead triple in the eighth
articles.summary: Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesda...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesday night.

Yainer Diaz hit a pair of solo homers, including a tying shot to the short porch in right field off Headrick's fastball to start the eighth. After Jeremy Pena singled, Alvarez ripped a low-inside sinker to the warning track in right-center for a 7-6 lead.

Alvarez increased his major league-leading batting average to .323. The slugger had his seventh career triple and first since July 21, 2024.

Pena homered off Fernando Cruz in the sixth for a 5-all tie. Daulton Varsho had two RBI singles for the Astros, who won for the sixth time in 15 games after owner Jim Crane said manager Joe Espada will finish the season.

Isaac Paredes added an RBI single off Headrick (7-3), who has allowed five homers in 68 appearances. Headrick is second in the big leagues in appearances to Toronto lefty Mason Fluharty and permitted a run for only the 12th time.

Diaz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth off rookie Bradley Hanner as the Astros scored six runs against New York's bullpen.

Houston overcame a four-hit night by New York first baseman Luis García Jr. García hit an RBI double off Steven Okert that gave the Yankees a 6-5 lead and also launched a two-run homer in the fifth off rookie starter Ethan Packo.

DETROIT (AP) — Max Clark hit his first home run at Comerica Park and five Detroit pitchers combined to allow one run as it ended a six-game losing streak with a win over Tampa Bay.

Clark's homer, the second of his career, gave the Tigers a 2-1 lead in the fifth inning, and that was more than enough for Detroit's pitching staff. Starter Jackson Jobe allowed one run in 4 1/3 innings, and four relievers combined to allow one hit.

Drew Sommers (1-3) retired all five batters he faced for his first major league victory and Kenley Jansen pitched the ninth for his 17th save.

Detroit had lost nine of its last 10 to fall 4 1/2 games behind Cleveland in the race for the third AL wild card.

Ian Seymour (9-5), who replaced Tampa Bay opener Casey Legumina , gave up four runs, three earned, on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings. The Rays have lost eight of their last 12 games.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Hunter Goodman homered in his return from a shoulder injury, Mason Adams worked into the fifth inning in his big league debut, and Colorado snapped a seven-game losing streak with a victory over Washington.

Daylen Lile went deep off Adams in the fourth, but that was all the scoring for Washington against six Colorado pitchers. Mark Manfredi (1-0) won in relief for his first career victory, and Jordan Romano worked the ninth for his 13th save in 16 chances.

Andrew Alvarez (2-6) allowed three runs and five hits in 4 2/3 innings with two walks and six strikeouts.

Playing for the first time in nearly two weeks, Goodman opened the scoring with a solo shot in the fourth, his 35th homer of the year. Connor Norby added an RBI double later that inning.

Lile's homer made it 2-1, but the Rockies restored a two-run lead when Jordan Beck scored all the way from second on a wild pitch. Alvarez covered the plate and received a throw from catcher Harry Ford before Beck came sliding in, but umpires ruled third baseman Brady House impeded Beck after he came around third, and the run was awarded.

TORONTO (AP) — Salvador Perez drove in two runs, Seth Lugo gave up one run in five effective innings, and Kansas City beat Toronto to extend its winning streak to nine games.

The last time the Kansas City Royals won nine straight was in July 2017.

Lugo (6-7) allowed six hits while striking out five to help the Royals take the first game of the three-game series.

Perez drove in the first run of the game despite grounding into a double play, then tacked on a go-ahead RBI single in the fifth for a 2-1 Kansas City lead. Kyle Isbel added insurance with an RBI sacrifice bunt, and Carter Jensen had a sacrifice fly in the sixth.

John Rave capped the scoring for the Royals with an RBI single in the ninth inning.

Max Scherzer (1-7) worked five innings, surrendering two runs on four hits for the Blue Jays. He struck out four and walked five while tying a season-high with 92 pitches. Scherzer is now within nine strikeouts of Gaylord Perry for ninth in major league history.

MIAMI (AP) — Jarren Duran hit a grand slam in the 11th inning, Mickey Gasper had his first career two-homer game and Boston beat Miami.

The surging Red Sox won their fifth in a row and ninth in 12 games. They have won their past three series and 14 of their last 20.

Willson Contreras led off the 11th with a single that advanced automatic runner Wilyer Abreu from second base to third. Jahmai Jones drew a walk to load the bases, and Abreu was forced out at home on Andruw Monasterio 's grounder.

Duran then connected on a sweeper from Cade Gibson (2-1) to put the Red Sox ahead 7-3. Alec Gamboa (1-0) tossed 1 1/3 hitless innings for his first major league win.

Gasper sent his first homer to right-center to put Boston up 1-0 in the second. It was the only run the Red Sox managed against starter Tyler Phillips , who struck out seven in 4 2/3 innings.

ATLANTA (AP) — Ozzie Albies singled in the go-ahead run with two outs in the eighth inning and Atlanta defeated Los Angles, snapping its six-game winning streak in a matchup of first-place clubs.

After the Braves squandered an early 3-0 lead against Tyler Glasnow , who made his first big league start in 3 1/2 months, Matt Olson led off the eighth with a double to left-center against Tanner Scott (1-4).

Mauricio Dubón moved the runner to third with a broken-bat grounder to second, but Michael Harris II failed to get Olson home with a weak grounder back to the mound. That left it up to Albies, who came through with a liner to center field.

Shohei Ohtani tripled off the left-field wall leading off the ninth against Raisel Iglesias , but the Dodgers couldn't get him home. Iglesias earned his 28th save in 31 chances.

Glasnow gave up hits to four of the first five Atlanta hitters, but the right-hander surrendered just two more during his five-inning stint. He struck out seven and didn't walk anyone while throwing 89 pitches.

ST. LOUIS (AP) — Pete Alonso had four hits, including a three-run homer, and drove in four runs before leaving the game in the fifth inning, and Baltimore routed swooning St. Louis.

Chris Bassitt (5-4) allowed one run on six hits in 6 2/3 innings, matching his longest start of the season. He struck out five and walked none as the Orioles, who are chasing an AL wild-card spot, won for the third time in four games.

The Cardinals lost their fourth straight.

Alonso, who has been dealing with a nagging calf injury, left shortly after he contributed his fourth hit, an RBI double during Baltimore's eight-run fifth that made it 12-1. He put the Orioles ahead 3-0 with his 435-foot shot in the third off Matthew Liberatore (5-12), his 31st of the season.

Jackson Holliday had three hits, scored twice and drove in a run for the Orioles in his first big league appearance in St. Louis, where his father, Matt, starred for the Cardinals. Christian Encarnacion-Strand had a pair of hits, including a 450-foot homer in the third, and drove in three. Leody Taveras had two hits, scored twice and drove in two runs.

Liberatore allowed a season-high eight runs on eight hits in four-plus innings. He struck out seven and walked one.

NEW YORK (AP) — Francisco Lindor made a diving catch at shortstop with the bases loaded in the ninth inning and scored the winning run on a throwing error in the 10th to lead New York past Milwaukee .

Lindor and Luis Robert Jr. homered for the last-place Mets (60-72), who are 13-6 since selling big at the trade deadline. Lindor's homer was his 154th for New York, tying Dave Kingman for sixth on the franchise list.

Carson Benge had his 11th three-hit game for the Mets, most among major league rookies.
